hero.title: OBJECTRADAR
hero.lead: Find nearby Bluetooth objects with intelligent BLE guidance

problem.title:
You know it's nearby.
But where is it?
problem.lead: You can know that a Bluetooth device is nearby without having a practical way to locate it precisely. ObjectRadar explores the Bluetooth information available to iOS to turn that signal into useful proximity guidance.

how-it-works.title: Three simple steps
how-it-works.lead: From scanning nearby Bluetooth devices, to identifying and tracking an object, ObjectRadar guides you through a simple workflow designed to help you find what you're looking for.

question1.question: What can the application detect?
question1.answer: ObjectRadar scans nearby Bluetooth Low Energy advertisements and analyzes the information made available by the devices. Detection depends on the device, its advertising behavior and the information exposed by its Bluetooth protocol.

question2.question: How does proximity guidance work?
question2.answer: The application observes changes in Bluetooth signal strength while you move. These changes can indicate whether you are getting closer to or farther from a device, but they cannot provide a precise distance.

question3.question: Why can some Bluetooth devices remain invisible?
question3.answer: A device may not advertise continuously, may use a protocol that does not expose enough information, or may be affected by Bluetooth and environmental limitations.

question4.question: What are the limitations of Bluetooth tracking?
question4.answer: Bluetooth signal strength is affected by distance, obstacles, reflections, device orientation and the surrounding environment. Proximity guidance should therefore be understood as an indication rather than an exact measurement.

tag.title: Find your Bluetooth tracker
tag.lead: You know your tracker is nearby, but you need help narrowing down where it is.

quote-box.title: THE LIMIT OF FIND MY PROTOCOL
quote-box.lead: Find My network can show the approximate location where a tracker was detected by a nearby Apple device, but it cannot tell you exactly where the tracker is inside your search area when precise finding is not supported.

tag.origin: ObjectRadar was created to help turn this approximate information into a practical local search.

compatibletrackers.title: Which trackers can you use?
compatibletrackers.lead: ObjectRadar is designed to detect Bluetooth trackers compatible with the Find My protocol and visible to iOS.
compatibletrackers.info-box-content:
An untested model does not mean that it is incompatible with ObjectRadar.
This list is not exhaustive and does not imply any partnership with the manufacturers or products listed.
User feedback about product compatibility is greatly appreciated and helps us keep this list up to date.

prerequisites.title: Understand what the indicators mean
prerequisites.lead: A few simple points will help you understand the search results.

position.title: POSITION
position.content: The location shown by Find My is the location of the device that detected the tracker. It is not necessarily the tracker's exact location.
position.question: Why can the displayed location be different?
position.answer: A tracker can be detected by a nearby Apple device. The reported location therefore gives you a useful starting area rather than an exact position.

approximate.title: Approximate location
approximate.content: The detecting iPhone does not give an exact tag position

detections.title: Several detections
detections.content: Multiple detections can narrow the search area, but do not prove an exact position

rssi.title: SIGNAL STRENGTH (RSSI)
rssi.content: RSSI indicates the relative strength of the Bluetooth signal. A stronger signal can help you determine whether you are moving in the right direction, but it cannot provide a reliable distance.
rssi.question: Why can the signal change unexpectedly?
rssi.answer: Walls, furniture, vehicles and other objects can affect Bluetooth signals. Compare several measurements instead of relying on a single reading.

move.title: Detect your tracker
move.content: Move slowly — Wait — Compare — Repeat — Take your time

timeinterval.title: TIME INTERVAL (FRAMES COMMUNICATION)
timeinterval.content: The tracker may not transmit continuously. The interval between two received advertising frames can vary.
timeinterval.question: What does the dot and the ring around the target mean?
timeinterval.answer:
The dot indicates the interval between received advertising frames.
Blue rings represent the search levels, while the two green levels indicate very close proximity. The ring color does not represent distance.

tip.title: SEARCHING AMONG SEVERAL TAGS
tip.content: If you own several tags, temporarily move the known tags away from the search area when possible. This reduces the number of nearby devices and makes it easier to identify the tag you are looking for

warning.title: NEARBY TAGS
warning.content: ObjectRadar may detect a Find My-compatible tag that does not belong to you. A detected tag is not necessarily your tag.

compatibility.title: COMPATIBILITY
compatibility.content: ObjectRadar is designed to detect Bluetooth trackers compatible with the Find My protocol and visible to iOS.
compatibility.question: Why might a tracker not be detected?
compatibility.answer: ObjectRadar cannot detect or display a device that is not compatible with the Find My protocol, is not authorized for use with it, or is filtered by iOS. ObjectRadar does not bypass Apple's device compatibility or access restrictions.

association.title: Search for an object, not a number
association.lead: ObjectRadar associates a detected tracker with an object you know.

objectassociation.title: OBJECTS ASSOCIATION WITH DEVICES
objectassociation.content: Instead of searching for an unknown Bluetooth device, you can search for an object such as your keys, bag or other personal item.
objectassociation.question: Why is this useful?
objectassociation.answer: A detected tracker is not automatically associated with an object. You can associate it with the object you believe it belongs to. If the association is incorrect, you can assign the object to another device at any time — before continuing the search or after discovering that you found the wrong item. ObjectRadar automatically updates the association.

rotatingidentifiers.title: ROTATING IDENTIFIERS
rotatingidentifiers.content: Some trackers periodically change the Bluetooth identifier used for advertising.
rotatingidentifiers.question: Why can a tracker temporarily disappear from the scan?
rotatingidentifiers.answer: A tracker may change its advertising identifier during a long search. Restarting the scan does not require you to associate the object again. When the same device UUID is detected again, its existing object association is retained.

step1.title: CHECK THE LAST KNOWN LOCATION
step1.lead: Before starting the local search, check the last known location of your tracker in Find My application. This can help you identify the area where you should start searching.
step1.info-box-content: You can also check whether the tracker reports a low battery.

step2.title: START SCAN
step2.lead: Press start button to discover devices around you.

step3.title: SELECT YOUR DEVICE
step3.lead: Select the device you are looking for from its identifier or its associated object.

step4.title: START THE TRACKING
step4.lead: Move slowly through the area and compare successive detections.
step4.info-box-content: Activating the sound will help you find the object without constantly looking at your iPhone when you are close to it.

step5.title: NARROW THE SEARCH AREA
step5.lead: Use successive detections and signal changes to progressively narrow the search area.

step6.title: OBJECT FOUND
step6.lead: When you are very close to the object the green circle will oscillate.
step6.info-box-content:
You found your object.
You can click the « Object found ? » button to stop the search and check how long it took to find the object.

limitations.title: What ObjectRadar cannot tell you
limitations.lead: Bluetooth performance depends on the environment and can affect the results of a search.

quote-box.title: PRECISIONS
quote-box.lead: ObjectRadar helps narrow the search area. It does not provide an exact GPS position or an exact distance to the tracker.

bluetooth.title: BLUETOOTH
bluetooth.content: Bluetooth signals are affected by the environment. RSSI should therefore be interpreted as an indication of relative signal strength, not as an exact distance.

battery.title: BATTERY
battery.content: A tracker with a very low battery may stop transmitting. If it no longer sends advertising frames, ObjectRadar cannot detect it.

rotating-identifiers.title: ROTATING IDENTIFIERS
rotating-identifiers.content: A tracker may temporarily disappear from the scan when its advertising identifier changes.

question1.question: Can ObjectRadar find any Bluetooth device?
question1.answer: ObjectRadar can detect nearby Bluetooth devices that are visible to iOS. Detection and identification depend on the information made available by the device and by iOS.

question2.question: Can ObjectRadar locate a Find My tracker exactly?
question2.answer: No. ObjectRadar helps narrow the search using Bluetooth detections and signal changes. It does not provide the exact physical position of the tracker.

question3.question: Why does the RSSI change?
question3.answer: Bluetooth signals are affected by distance, obstacles, reflections and the surrounding environment. Compare several measurements rather than relying on a single RSSI value.

question4.question: Why should I move slowly?
question4.answer: Moving slowly gives the tracker time to transmit new advertising frames and gives you more measurements to compare.

question5.question: Why can a tracker disappear during a search?
question5.answer: A tracker may temporarily change its identifier or simply not be detected during a scan interval or becoming out of range. Restarting the scan may help find it again.

question6.question: Can ObjectRadar decrypt Find My data?
question6.answer: No. ObjectRadar does not decrypt or access encrypted Find My data. It works with the Bluetooth information available to the application through iOS.

question7.question: Can I correct an object association?
question7.answer: Yes. You can correct an association at any time, including after discovering that the detected device was associated with the wrong object.

hearing.title: Find a misplaced hearing aid
hearing.lead: ObjectRadar helps you locate a Bluetooth hearing aid nearby when you cannot immediately find it.

quote-box.title: THE LIMIT OF HEARING AID
quote-box.lead: Unlike a Bluetooth tracker designed to be detected by nearby devices, a hearing aid is normally associated with its user's iPhone. ObjectRadar uses the Bluetooth connection available from that iPhone to help you search for the hearing aid locally.

compatiblehearings.title: Which hearing aids can be searched?
compatiblehearings.lead: ObjectRadar is designed for hearing aids with Bluetooth connectivity that can be discovered by iOS.
compatiblehearings.content: Compatibility depends on the hearing aid model, its Bluetooth capabilities and the information made available to iOS. The list of tested models is not exhaustive.
compatiblehearings.info-box-content:
Compatibility depends on the hearing aid model, its Bluetooth capabilities and the information made available to iOS.
An untested model does not mean that it is incompatible with ObjectRadar.
This list is not exhaustive and does not imply any partnership with the manufacturers or products listed.
User feedback about product compatibility is greatly appreciated and helps us keep this list up to date.

prerequisites.title: Check the Bluetooth connection
prerequisites.lead: The search relies on the Bluetooth connection between your iPhone and your hearing aid.

pairing.title: PAIRING
pairing.content: Your hearing aid should already be associated with the iPhone you are using for the search. A hearing aid paired with another device may not be available to ObjectRadar.

discovery.title: Searching for already paired hearing aids
discovery.content: To see your hearing aids in ObjectRadar, they must first be paired with your iPhone and connected

pairing.question: Why does the paired iPhone matter?
pairing.answer: The iPhone is the device that communicates with and discovers the hearing aid. This is different from a Bluetooth tracker that can be detected by nearby devices.

bluetooth.title: BLUETOOTH
bluetooth.content: ObjectRadar uses the Bluetooth information available to iOS to identify and search for the hearing aid.
bluetooth.question: How does the signal help me find it?
bluetooth.answer: As with Bluetooth trackers, the RSSI value can help you determine whether the signal is getting stronger or weaker as you move. It does not provide a reliable distance.

association.title: Search for an object, not a number
association.lead: ObjectRadar associates a detected hearing with an object you know.
association.learnMore: Learn more about hearing aids association (link)

objectassociation.title: OBJECTS ASSOCIATION WITH DEVICES
objectassociation.content: You can associate each hearing aid (left and right) with a personnal object with a custum label
objectassociation.question: Why is this useful?
objectassociation.answer: A detected hearing aid is not automatically associated with an object. You can associate it with the object you believe it belongs to. If the association is incorrect, you can assign the object to another hearing at any time — before continuing the search or after discovering that you found the wrong item. ObjectRadar automatically updates the association.

rotatingidentifiers.title: ROTATING IDENTIFIERS
rotatingidentifiers.content: A paired hearing aid may keep the same Bluetooth UUID for a long period, but iOS may assign a different UUID in some situations.
rotatingidentifiers.question: Why can a hearing aid temporarily disappear from the scan?
rotatingidentifiers.answer: If the UUID changes, ObjectRadar will detect the hearing aid as a new device. In this case, the object association should be modified manually. When the same device UUID is detected again, its existing object association is retained.

steps.title: How to find your hearing aid

step1.title: CHECK THE BLUETOOTH CONNECTION
step1.lead: Make sure Bluetooth is enabled and that the hearing aid is associated with the iPhone you are using.
step1.info-box-content:
Paired: means that your iPhone knows and is authorized to communicate with the hearing aid.
Connected: means that the hearing aid is currently communicating with your iPhone.
step1.content-paired-connected: Before starting a local search with ObjectRadar, the hearing aid must already be paired with your iPhone and currently connected to it.

quote-box.title: TAG VS HEARING AID
quote-box.lead:
With a Find My tracker, Find My app can provide an approximate location based on the Find My network.
With a hearing aid, ObjectRadar relies on the current Bluetooth connection with your iPhone to confirm that the hearing aid is available for a local search.

step2.title: START SCAN
step2.lead: Press start button to discover hearing aid around you.

step3.title: SELECT YOUR HEARING AID
step3.lead: Select the detected hearing aid you are looking for from its identifier or its associated object.

step4.title: START THE TRACKING
step4.lead: Move slowly through the area and compare successive detections.
step4.info-box-content: Activating the sound will help you find the object without constantly looking at your iPhone when you are close to it.

step5.title: NARROW THE SEARCH AREA
step5.lead: Use successive detections and signal changes to progressively narrow the search area.

step6.title: OBJECT FOUND
step6.lead: When you are very close to the object the green circle will oscillate.
step6.info-box-content:
You found your hearing.
You can click the « Object found ? » button to stop the search and check how long it took to find the object.

limitations.title: What can affect the search?
limitations.lead: Bluetooth detection depends on the hearing aid, its state and the surrounding environment.

quote-box.title: PRECISIONS
quote-box.lead: ObjectRadar helps narrow the search area. It does not provide an exact GPS position or an exact distance to the hearing aid.

bluetooth.title: BLUETOOTH
bluetooth.content: Bluetooth range depends on the hearing aid, the iPhone, obstacles and radio conditions. A hearing aid may temporarily become difficult to detect even when it is nearby.

battery.title: BATTERY
battery.content: The hearing aid must have enough battery power to maintain its Bluetooth functionality. A switched-off or discharged hearing aid cannot be located through Bluetooth.

rotating-identifiers.title: ROTATING IDENTIFIERS
rotating-identifiers.content: During our tests, the Bluetooth UUID of a hearing aid remained stable for a long period. However, this behavior may vary depending on the model, its state and its configuration. ObjectRadar therefore does not assume that all hearing aids use a permanently fixed identifier.

question1.question: Why can the signal change unexpectedly?
question1.answer: Walls, furniture, the human body and other radio conditions can affect Bluetooth signal strength.

question2.question: Can I search for a hearing aid with another iPhone?
question2.answer: The search is intended to use the iPhone associated with the hearing aid. A different iPhone may not be able to discover or identify it in the same way.

question3.question: Why is my hearing aid not detected?
question3.answer: The hearing aid may not be compatible with the Bluetooth information available to ObjectRadar, may not be associated with the iPhone, may be switched off, or may be temporarily unavailable, for example because it is out of range.

question4.question: Does ObjectRadar show the exact distance to my hearing aid?
question4.answer: No. Bluetooth signal strength can help you search progressively, but RSSI should not be interpreted as an exact distance.
